Blend Approach 2: round 8's own iterative-elimination ablation loop, re-run from scratch seeded with Task #93's full 17-name SURVIVING_INDICATORS pool (round 8 itself started from a narrower pool), carrying Round 2's extra_windows fix throughout. It is not published to digiquant.io and settings.json was never modified.

Ablation loop ran 8 rounds (stopped at budget_exhausted, the MAX_ROUNDS cap). Best-seen was round 1 -- the very first reweight of the full 17-name pool, before anything was eliminated -- dominated by power_law, onchain_addr_ratio, and weekly_monthly_macd (each weight=1.0), everything else in the pool at a floor 0.1. Every later round (dropping the prior round's dominant indicator) scored worse, several sharply negative -- broadening the pool did not surface anything better than round 8's own narrower search.

Walk-forward vs. flat DCA: mean_oos_vs_flat_dca_pct(unweighted)=+3.52%, mean_oos_vs_flat_dca_pct(duration)=+3.52%, beats_flat_dca_oos=True. Walk-forward vs. the risk50-linear baseline: delta_mean_oos_vs_flat_dca_pct=+38.96%, beats_baseline_oos=True. It FAILED the sensitivity-neighbor stability gate (max_abs_delta_oos_pct=6.03 vs a 2.0 threshold) -- verdict is Not Promoted.

Comparison: roughly matches Task #93 Round 2's own weak magnitude (+4.07% OOS) but with worse instability (6.03 vs 2.79), and is far below round 8 (+52.01% OOS, numerically beats flat DCA but fails sensitivity). The full 17-indicator pool converges on essentially the same power_law-dominant shape seen elsewhere in this research line, not a new edge.
